title: Localization comparisons in a field tower
statement:
Let $k\to L\to H$ be a tower of field extensions [def-pc-field-extension], $R$ a commutative $k$-algebra, $S=R\otimes_kL$, and $T=R\otimes_kH$. Tensor products have multiplication $(r\otimes a)(s\otimes b)=rs\otimes ab$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Write $j:S\to T$ for $r\otimes l\mapsto r\otimes l$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ and $\mathfrak p$ its inverse image in $R$. Set $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=S_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $V=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, and $U=S\setminus\mathfrak q$. There are canonical compatible identifications
$$A\otimes_kH\cong V^{-1}T,\qquad B\otimes_LH\cong j(U)^{-1}T.$$
The induced map $A\otimes_kH\to B\otimes_LH$ is a localization at the images of $U$ under $S\to T\to V^{-1}T$. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak Q$ of $T$ with $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q$, the canonical map $B\otimes_LH\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ is a further localization at the images of $T\setminus\mathfrak Q$. All maps agree on $T$: the last map sends a fraction $t/j(u)$ to the same fraction in $T_{\mathfrak Q}$. The identifications respect the structural maps from $R$, $L$, and $H$ wherever defined. No finiteness or Noetherianity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), proof of (3): factor the local-ring map through scalar extension and then localize; applied to the tower k to L to H.

proof.text: Identify $S\otimes_LH$ with $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-transitive], applied to $k\to L\to H$ and $M=R$: $\theta((r\otimes l)\otimes h)=r\otimes lh$, with inverse $r\otimes h\mapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes h$. These are ring maps: on two pure tensors the product formula of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives $rs\otimes ll' hh'$ on both sides, and both maps send $1$ to $1$; additivity then gives multiplicativity on all elements. Under $\theta$, $s\otimes1$ maps to $j(s)$.

source.place: Tags 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule) and 00CX (lemma-tensor-product); the multiplication is the one in the item.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] to the base ring $k$, algebra and module $R$, multiplicative subset $V$, and module $H$. It gives an additive isomorphism $V^{-1}T\to A\otimes_kH$, $(r\otimes h)/v\mapsto(r/v)\otimes h$. Its inverse sends $(r/v)\otimes h$ to $(r\otimes h)/(v\otimes1)$. This inverse preserves products: the product of $(r/v)\otimes h$ and $(r'/v')\otimes h'$ goes to $(rr'\otimes hh')/((vv')\otimes1)$, the product of their images; it preserves $1$. Fractions generate $A$ additively, so these checks prove the ring identification. Here and below $V^{-1}T$ means localization at $M=\{v\otimes1:v\in V\}\subset T$.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), combined with 00D2 as in the cited node; fraction multiplication from Section 00CM.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] to the base ring $L$, algebra and module $S$, subset $U$, and module $H$. This identifies $B\otimes_LH$ with the localization of $S\otimes_LH$ at $u\otimes1$ for $u\in U$. The map is $(s/u)\otimes h\mapsto(s\otimes h)/(u\otimes1)$; the product of $(s/u)\otimes h$ and $(s'/u')\otimes h'$ maps to $(ss'\otimes hh')/((uu')\otimes1)$, the product of their images, and $1$ maps to $1$. Additivity extends this to all elements. Transport by $\theta$ from step 1 gives $B\otimes_LH\cong N^{-1}T$ with $N=j(U)$, sending $(s/u)\otimes h$ to $j(s)(1\otimes h)/j(u)$.

source.place: Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization) and 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule); varieties Tag 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), proof of (3).

proof.text: If $v\in V$, then $v\otimes1\notin\mathfrak q$ by the definition $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. Thus $M\subseteq N$. The map $A\to B$, $r/v\mapsto(r\otimes1)/(v\otimes1)$, exists by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]. Together with $H\to B\otimes_LH$, it induces $A\otimes_kH\to B\otimes_LH$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The formulas in steps 2 and 3 show that its composite with $T\to M^{-1}T$ is $T\to N^{-1}T$: on $r\otimes h$ both give $(r\otimes h)/1$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], with ring $T$ and subsets $M\subseteq N$, now says this map is localization at the images of $N=j(U)$ in $M^{-1}T$.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization); transitivity in Section 00CM, made explicit by the cited localization-of-localization node.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak Q\subset T$ with $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q$ and set $P=T\setminus\mathfrak Q$. Every $u\in U$ has $j(u)\notin\mathfrak Q$, so $N\subseteq P$. In particular the map $T\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ sends all of $N$ to units. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] it extends uniquely to $N^{-1}T\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$, $t/j(u)\mapsto(t/1)(j(u)/1)^{-1}$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], now for $N\subseteq P$, proves that this is localization at the images of $P$, as asserted. Under step 3 this is the canonical map out of $B\otimes_LH$.

The displayed maps agree on $T$ by their numerator formulas. Equality on pure tensors gives equality on the whole tensor product by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], and equality on $T$ extends uniquely across either denominator set by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]. The structural elements from $R$, $L$, and $H$ are respectively $r\otimes1$, $1\otimes l$, and $1\otimes h$ in $T$ (with $l$ mapped into $H$). All formulas preserve these elements and hence all the asserted structural maps. This also proves compatibility of the two identifications with both localization arrows.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization) and the tensor-product universal property, Tag 00CX.
